_comment: Entra Policy Suite 2.0 guided install: every answer is a PARAMETER of tools/setup/Install-EntraPolicySuite.ps1 (and passed on unchanged by the launcher Start-EpsInstall.ps1). -TenantId and -SubscriptionId are required; every other answer takes its default. Entra Policy Suite installs Community, unlicensed; a licence is added in the product after sign-in. No licence, key, hash or config file is ever part of the install lines. The 'installer' block is what the Invardia portal builds the two install lines from: line 1 per edition (INSTALL-1 / INS-02: GitHub for Community, invardia.com/support/eps/ for Pro), line 2 the same for both. tests/Test-EpsNetwork.ps1 keeps this file in step with the installer's and the launcher's parameter blocks.

installer.urlFrom: Community: the public GitHub release (latestUrl / pinnedUrlTemplate); Pro: invardia.com (proUrl)
installer.runsIn: PowerShell 7 or Azure Cloud Shell; a browser sign-in; no modules, no Azure CLI

parameters.help: Your Microsoft Entra tenant id.

The Azure subscription Entra Policy Suite is installed in. You need Owner on it (or on an existing resource group), and Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator in Entra for the Graph and Exchange grants.
The Azure region.
The resource group; created when it does not exist. Empty: rg-eps for a new install, or rg-entrapolicysuite when an install made before 2.0.55 is there.
The install journal (a stopped install resumes from it) and the network hand-off. Empty: ~/clouddrive/invardia/eps-<subscription> in Cloud Shell, else ~/invardia/eps-<subscription>.
The Azure SQL server's region when Azure SQL does not take new servers in the install's region. Empty: the install's region.
Your Entra security group to be the Azure SQL server's admin (you must be a member). Empty: you. An existing server keeps its admin.
The display name of that group.
The update ring this install belongs to (0-10), reported on the heartbeat. Invardia tells you the ring. Empty: a re-run keeps the install's ring.
A Graph permission of the engine your approver did not approve: it is never granted, and the feature that needs it reports its data as unavailable.
Print less while installing.

Off (default): the web app has a public address behind the Entra sign-in; the database, Key Vault, job queues and registry use their public endpoints, protected by Entra sign-in and managed identities. On: everything runs in your virtual network - the Container Apps environment has no public address (the web app is reachable from your network only), and the database, Key Vault, job queues and registry (Premium) are created with public access off and reached through private endpoints and private DNS zones. Run a private install from a machine inside your network.
Your existing virtual network, in the same region (the install needs Network Contributor on it). Empty: the install makes its own network from the range below.
Only without a network id: the range of the network the install makes (at least a /25). Its subnets are then the first /26 (the environment) and the second /26 (the private endpoints).
Only without a network id: the name of the network the install makes.
The subnet of the Container Apps environment: at least a /27, delegated to Microsoft.App/environments. Created when it is not there; an existing empty subnet is delegated.
Its range, only when the subnet is created. Empty in a network the install makes: the first /26.
The subnet of the private endpoints and the registry's build pool (no delegation). Created when it is not there.
Its range, only when the subnet is created. Empty in a network the install makes: the second /26.

The resource group of your central private DNS zones. Its zones are used, never created, and nothing is written there; a missing zone is on the network hand-off list. Empty: the zones are made in the install's resource group and linked to the network. The web app's own zone always stays in the install's resource group.
Your hub network (may be in another subscription). Nothing is written there by default: it makes the hand-off list exact and gives your hub owner a script to run.
Link the install's DNS zones to the hub - only when you may join the hub network (checked before any change).
Peer the network with the hub in both directions - only when you may on both networks (checked before any change). Never half a peering.

Your internal address ranges that reach the web app through your hub firewall (e.g. 10.0.0.0/8). With the firewall address, on a network the install makes, the apps subnet gets a return route (rt-eps) to the firewall - without it the replies time out. On your own network the route is on the hand-off list.
Your hub firewall's private address: the next hop of the return route for your internal ranges.

options.label: From the internet, behind Entra sign-in

parameters.help: A private network install is always internal.
Only when the install cannot prove a private install from inside your network: you checked the web app from a machine in your network yourself.

Your Invardia Support app, named by its client id (never found by name). It starts with the support level below until your organization's level from the Invardia portal arrives. Without it, the install grants the Support app nothing.
The Support app's starting level: troubleshoot or setup (read, plus admin only during an open support session of at most 8 hours), read, or none. Used only with -SupportAppId.
Continue an interrupted install with the same values: finished steps are skipped. Refused when there is no interrupted install.

requiredRights: Owner on the subscription (or on an existing resource group, with the resource providers registered)
Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator in Entra (the engine's Graph and Exchange permissions, the web sign-in registration)
Private network with your own network: Network Contributor on it; -PeerToHub / -LinkZonesToHub: Network Contributor on the hub
